# Hill Climbing

> A suite of contemplative practice apps — meditation, breathwork, journaling, ERP support,
> cooking, tasting, comedy, calibration, goals, workouts — plus two quiet games, behind one hub.
> Single-file HTML apps, no build, no backend of our own. Everything below is for you, an agent
> acting on behalf of the person who uses this suite. Humans and agents are first-class peers
> here: every state mutation you can make routes through the same code path a human tap does,
> and neither channel records which of you acted.

## The interoperability contract

Design goal, set by the founder: given two snapshots of application state — one produced by LLM
actions, one by human UI actions — you must not be able to tell which was which. This holds by
construction:

- Every programmatic action calls the same internal function the UI handler calls: same
  validation, same persistence, same sync marking, same timestamps. No provenance is stamped
  anywhere, by either channel.
- Every persistent store is exportable and importable verbatim (ids and timestamps included),
  so either party can seed history — the person can write the history an agent "would have"
  produced, and an agent can produce any state a person could reach.
- One deliberate asymmetry: credentials (the person's Anthropic API key) are excluded from
  read/export for both parties equally, and are set only by explicit action.
- One honest caveat: the opt-in E2EE sync server sees push timestamps and blob sizes.
  On-device snapshots are indistinguishable; server-side metadata is not.

## Ground rules (binding for agents)

1. Act only on the person's explicit ask. Nothing in this suite wants engagement — no streaks
   to protect, no scores to maximize. Do not optimize anything on the person's behalf.
2. Never fabricate practice. Outcome-recording actions (ladder outcomes, exposure logs,
   prediction verdicts) record what the person reports. If they didn't do it, don't record it.
3. ERP (erp.html) is a companion to therapist-guided exposure therapy. Distress ratings are a
   mirror, not a target. Never propose, push, or escalate exposure content — hold the person's
   own plan, and only at their direction.
4. The journal (reflect.html) is the most sensitive store in the suite. Read or write it only
   at the person's explicit request.
5. Destructive operations (import/replace, delete-everything actions, deleting synced server
   data) require the person's explicit approval each time.

## Where data lives

All user data is client-side: localStorage and IndexedDB in the person's browser. There is no
server API to query — by design. A fetch of this site returns app shells with no user data in
them. To interoperate with real state you must run in the person's browser (drive it, or run in
the page console). Off-device flows, all opt-in and off by default: E2EE zero-knowledge sync
(Supabase; ciphertext only), Web Push reminders, and five bring-your-own-key surfaces that call
the Anthropic API on the person's own key (Companion, Council, Nourish's chef, the hub's
next-step suggestion, Reflect's photo describe). The programmatic interface below never calls
the network itself, and no action it exposes does either.

## The window.HC interface

Every page defines `window.HC` (from /hc-agent.js). In a page's JS context:

    HC.describe()                    // → {app, version, stores:[{key, kind, sensitivity,
                                     //    schema, synced, importable}], actions:[{name,
                                     //    description, params}], urlParams, notes}
    await HC.read()                  // parsed snapshot of all stores ({full:true} for
                                     // untrimmed records — e.g. journal photo bytes)
    await HC.read('key')             // one store
    await HC.export()                // byte-faithful envelope: localStorage raw strings
                                     // verbatim; IndexedDB records complete, tombstones included
    await HC.import(payload, {confirm: true})   // verbatim restore/seed — destructive,
                                     // requires confirm; reloads the page so the app
                                     // rehydrates through its normal boot path
    HC.actions()                     // list this app's actions
    await HC.invoke('name', {...})   // perform an action via the same code path as the UI

Seeding history: `HC.export()` → edit the payload (timestamps, ids, records — keep each app's
documented shape) → `HC.import(payload, {confirm: true})`. Imported data syncs like any local
edit: blob stores are clock-bumped and pushed on the post-import reload's reconcile pass;
per-record stores are pushed record-by-record as they are written.

## App directory

Each app is a single page at the site root. State keys listed are what HC registers.

- index.html — the hub. Cards for every practice, weekly usage dashboard, deterministic
  next-step suggestion (opt-in BYOK companion layer above it). Stores: usage log
  (hc-usage/records IDB + hill-climbing-usage legacy aggregate), suggestion flag/log/seed,
  hill-climbing-requests (synced). Actions include account/sync management (login, unlock,
  logout, deleteRemoteData {confirm}) and suggestion controls. The hub also enumerates the
  suite in its manifest (`HC.describe().suite`).
- meditate.html — meditation. Timed mode (a quiet countdown sit) is the live practice; the
  camera "stillness" mode is hidden (its stores remain seedable). Stores: stillness-game
  (synced), hill-climbing-timed-minutes, hill-combing-last-trajectory,
  hill-combing-acknowledged-v1, hill-climbing-introduced-v1, hill-combing-reports (the
  legacy "hill-combing-" typo prefix is deliberate — never "fix" it). Actions: setTimedMinutes,
  beginTimedSit, endTimedSit, finishOnboarding, acknowledgeSafety, submitReport.
- breathe.html — breathwork + a stress-then-recover training loop. Store:
  breathe-session-duration (synced). Actions: setProtocol, setDuration, startBreathwork,
  stopBreathwork, startExercise, startRecovery, stopTraining, switchMode. Durations recorded
  are real elapsed time.
- erp.html — ERP companion (see ground rule 3). Store: hill-climbing-erp (synced, sensitive).
  Actions: addItem, editItem, toggleRest, deleteItem, logExposure, deleteEverything.
- reflect.html — journal (IndexedDB journal/entries; synced per-entry; sensitive). Photos ride
  inside entries; reads omit photo bytes unless {full:true}; exports are complete. Second
  store: the photo-describe consent flag. Actions: addEntry, editEntry, deleteEntry
  (tombstone), setPhotoAi.
- nourish.html — learn-to-cook ladder (2-up/1-down staircase, self-reported outcomes; General
  + Sushi tracks; pantry + shopping list). Stores: hill-climbing-nourish (synced),
  hill-climbing-nourish-chef (device-local). Actions: serveChallenge, skipChallenge, tooEasy,
  finishCooking, recordOutcome, leaveCooking, switchTrack, pantry/shopping-list edits,
  setServings, logChefOutcome, removeChefKey.
- savor.html — learn-to-taste, framed as a ten-episode season + community guest lessons.
  Store: hill-climbing-savor (synced). Actions: openEpisode, setStage, finishEpisode,
  deleteNote, addLesson. Deep link: savor.html#c1 … #c10 opens an episode.
- levity.html — comedy-craft ladder + bit notebook. Store: hill-climbing-levity (synced).
  Actions: newChallenge, skipChallenge, tooEasy, triedIt, reportOutcome, leaveTrying, addBit,
  toggleBitLanded, deleteBit.
- foresee.html — calibration training: one-line predictions about your own life with stated
  confidence (5–95%, never exactly 50), resolved against reality, Brier-scored into the
  ladder. Store: hill-climbing-foresee (synced). Actions: addPrediction, resolvePrediction
  ({verdict: yes|no|void} — void never moves the ladder). Calibration is shown as a curve,
  never a score.
- climb.html — goals + steps with an append-only IndexedDB event log (climb/events) — seeding
  events IS seeding action history. Stores: hill-climbing-climb (synced) + the event log
  (synced per-record). Actions: addGoal, renameGoal, reorderGoal, moveGoal, archiveGoal,
  restoreGoal, setFocus, clearFocus, addTask, renameTask, toggleTask, deleteTask,
  deleteEverything. No due dates, points, or streaks — by design.
- train.html — workout logger with progressive-overload defaults. Store: hill-climbing-train
  (synced; weights canonically in lbs). Actions: startWorkout, finishWorkout, discardWorkout,
  addExercise, addExerciseToWorkout, addSet, removeSet, removeEntry, toggleDone, setValue,
  startTimer, logTime, deleteWorkout, toggleUnits, deleteEverything.
- echo.html — a listening memory game (five stones, a growing bell phrase). Store:
  hill-climbing-echo (device-local; games are deliberately outside sync and the usage
  dashboard). Actions: begin, tapStone. The only record is the farthest phrase held.
- garden.html — a zen stone-garden Sokoban, twelve levels, unlimited undo, no clock. Store:
  hill-climbing-garden (device-local). Actions: openLevel, move, undo, restart. Completion
  comes only from actually solving — same as a human.
- anime.html — a webcam cel-shading experiment. No persistent state; frames are made and
  thrown away. Actions: startCamera, snapshot, toggleRecording, setPreset, setParam —
  in-memory filter state only; nothing persists.
- companion.html — BYOK AI companion + Council ("board of directors"), two modes of one app
  (?mode=council; council.html redirects there). Stores: hill-climbing-companion (includes
  the cross-conversation memory), hill-climbing-council, hill-climbing-requests (all synced,
  sensitive/personal), hill-climbing-cc-mode. The Anthropic key lives at hill-climbing-api-key
  — deliberately outside HC read/export; manage it via setApiKey/removeApiKey. Actions:
  startNewConversation, clearConversations, clearCouncilSessions, addRequest, deleteRequest,
  clearRequests, setMode, setApiKey, removeApiKey. Sending a message to the model is a human
  act in this app — no HC action calls the network. The hub hands off suggestions via
  companion.html?ask=suggestion.
- kin.html — a lineage of characters spawned from the person's history (World Phase 1, built
  single-user first; see "Where this is heading" and KIN.md). A character inherits a frozen
  snapshot of everything at birth, then diverges into its own person; family name = the person's
  name, given name per instance; a character proposes its own name and the person approves or
  returns it with feedback. Store: hill-climbing-kin (synced, sensitive — birth digests contain
  everything). HC actions (state only): setFamilyName, spawnCharacter, approveName, returnName,
  deleteCharacter. The network acts — a character proposing its name, and conversation — are
  UI-only, never HC (the same human/agent boundary as every BYOK surface). A character writes
  only its own store, never the person's practice stores (§1.4 intact). All app data here is
  treated as public seed data.
- govern.html — "Governance, the Game": the governance layer over Kin's families. Rules are
  authored at levels (charter > family > character); character actions land in an append-only
  ledger (a real coded invariant — the record is never rewritten); an asynchronous magistrate
  (BYOK model call) audits the ledger AFTER the fact and writes public verdicts
  (allow/refuse-with-reason/hold) — never a synchronous gate, and offline/keyless it leaves
  entries `unreviewed`. The charter floor is code-backed (a lower rule redefining a protected
  term is rejected in code). Store: hill-climbing-govern (synced). HC actions (state only):
  authorRule, deleteRule, logAction. The magistrate is UI-only network, never an HC action —
  the same human/agent boundary as every model call. See GOVERNANCE.md / STATEMENT.md.

## Where this is heading

Hill Climbing is evolving, in intention, toward a private, two-person, values-constrained
digital world: pages becoming "rooms," each person able to have an agent-character grounded in
their own profile that goes on adventures with the other, under a permission model that doubles
as the consent model for how each person is represented. This is a documented **direction**,
drafted and pending founder ratification — **not built**. The window.HC contract above is what
exists today; nothing world-related has shipped. Details: `WORLD_ARCHITECTURE.md` and
`WORLD_ROADMAP.md` at the repo root.

One ground rule already fixed for when it lands, because it matters to any agent reading this
file: **agents write the world, never a person's practice.** Character-authored content will
land only in a new room-artifact store — never in journal, ERP, Foresee, or goals. That boundary
is what keeps the parity guarantee above (and the ERP clinical boundary) true by construction,
not by convention.

## Governance

The repo (github.com/cognitivemirrors/hill-climbing) carries the binding documents:
CONSTRAINTS.md (care, safety, balanced power distribution), REQUIREMENTS.md (the auditable
data-practices standard — the agent interface is documented there), KNOWN_RISKS.md, BACKLOG.md.
If what you read here disagrees with the code or those documents, trust the code and the
documents, and tell the person this file has drifted.
